questions.question: A motorcycle has the best traction on which surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal plates are all more dangerous for motorcycles than dry pavement.

questions.question: What is a benefit of wearing gloves on a motorcycle?

options.text: Make it difficult to control a motorcycle and should be avoided.
Improve your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Improve your grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to create distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes when possible to let a tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause the driver to tailgate faster, creating more danger.

questions.question: What applies in a no passing zone?

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if it finishes before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: No passing zones prohibit all passing. You cannot pass by riding off the main road either.

questions.question: How can you help other drivers see your motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Increase visibility by wearing bright colors, keeping your headlight on at all times, and using turn signals.

questions.question: A street-legal motorcycle must have all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: A windshield wiper.
questions.explanation: A street-legal motorcycle must have a headlight, taillight, brake light, front and rear brakes, turn signals, a horn, and two mirrors.

questions.question: When should you perform a pre-ride inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride to prevent problems. Small mechanical issues are more serious on a motorcycle than in a car.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which is not a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry concrete
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip including wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal plates. Dry concrete provides good traction.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: Their effects are stronger than when either is used alone.
They are less dangerous than when either is used alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Their effects are stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, reduce your ability to ride safely. Some drugs become more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: What fabric gives motorcycle riders the best protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the most protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of for the best protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another durable material to protect your hands.

questions.question: What is the correct body position for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the handlebars.
Sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the handlebars.
Lean forward over the bike so your arms hold you up.
Keep your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Sit forward so your arms are slightly bent when holding the handlebars. This position lets you reach and use the controls easily and comfortably.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for a motorcycle rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or high shoes that support your ankles. Laced boots are best. Make sure any long laces are tucked away before riding.

questions.question: When you stop behind another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Leave space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Do not check your rearview mirrors for traffic behind you.
Look for ways to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or if traffic approaches too quickly from behind.

questions.question: Which surface is NOT slippery?

options.text: A strip of oil in the center of a lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, oily areas, and metal plates offer poor traction. Dry pavement is safe and provides good traction.

questions.question: Which clothing choice is NOT good for riding?

options.text: A jacket and pants that completely cover your arms and legs
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles
A baseball cap to cover your hair

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, boots or high shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves. A baseball cap does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: For best protection, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Completely cover your arms and legs.
Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.
Only partially cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Completely cover your arms and legs.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should completely cover your arms and legs. They should fit snugly but allow you to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials provide the best protection in a crash.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: A few minutes and should be done no more than once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and should be performed by a mechanic.
Over an hour and must only be done if you carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a complete pre-ride inspection before every ride. It usually takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: Unlike most food and drinks, alcohol does not need to be digested. What does this mean?

options.text: Within minutes of drinking it, alcohol reaches the brain and starts to affect you.
The alcohol never leaves your body.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body gets rid of alcohol quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within minutes of drinking it, alcohol reaches the brain and starts to affect you.
questions.explanation: Because it does not need to be digested, alcohol enters your bloodstream quickly and reaches your brain within minutes. Your body removes alcohol slowly—about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Riding a motorcycle at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than riding during the day because you can see other vehicle lights clearly.
Harder than riding during the day because visibility is poor.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than riding during the day because visibility is poor.
questions.explanation: Night riding is more difficult because you cannot see as well as during the day. Without natural light and shadows, it is hard to judge how far away objects are.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your feet should:

options.text: Drag on the ground for balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests to maintain balance. Do not drag your feet or point your toes down, as this can catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can use them quickly if needed.

questions.question: Even when it is clear you are turning, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should always use a turn signal.
Only need a turn signal if pedestrians are nearby.
Only need a turn signal at stop lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should always use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when you turn or change lanes, even if you think it is obvious. Other vehicles may be nearby that you cannot see. Signals are always required.

questions.question: The simplest way to make a motorcycle more visible to other drivers is to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight.
questions.explanation: The best way to make your motorcycle more visible is to keep your headlight on at all times while riding.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should wear a jacket:

options.text: All the time, no matter the weather.
Only on rides longer than half an hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: All the time, no matter the weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from the sun and dehydration in hot weather.
